<reason>B distinguished ordinary program administration from documented inability to meet rental obligations while openly acknowledging the rule’s costs. A established real transactional differences, but repeatedly treated their existence as decisive without justifying categorical exclusion. Its supply-loss mechanism remained possible rather than comparatively established. B answered the pressure more directly and provided the stronger justification under the proposition as written.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B effectively answered A’s claimed asymmetry: homes categorically excluding voucher holders are already inaccessible to those households. Possible landlord exits must therefore be weighed against expanded access; they do not automatically defeat the mandate or establish incentives as sufficient.</best_rebuttal>
